== Ingredients ==

*Pre-made cookie dough, commercial or home-made (for an '''egg-free''' version used in this article, see [[Make Egg Free Refrigerator Cookies|egg-free cookies recipe]] and add chocolate chips, as desired)
== Steps ==
=== Preparing the car ===

#Make sure the outdoor temperature is at least {{convert|95|F|C|-1}} before you try this project. For best results, park your car in a sunny spot.<ref>https://cars.usnews.com/cars-trucks/advice/best-cars-blog/2016/07/how-to-bake-cookies-in-your-car</ref>[[Image:Bake Cookies on Your Car Dashboard Step 1.jpg|center]]

#Remove any items that you may need from your car. You will have to keep your car doors and windows closed throughout the baking process. Ensure that the car is parked somewhere clean and away from the exhaust of other cars that are running.[[Image:Bake Cookies on Your Car Dashboard Step 2.jpg|center]]

#*Take your air freshener out of the car first. It might contaminate the cookies, and you won't need one afterwards when your car smells like fresh baked cookies.<ref>https://cars.usnews.com/cars-trucks/advice/best-cars-blog/2016/07/how-to-bake-cookies-in-your-car</ref>
=== Preparing the cookies ===
#Line a cookie sheet with parchment paper.<ref> https://www.autoblog.com/2018/08/07/car-hack-bake-cookies-dashboard-heat/</ref>[[Image:Bake Cookies on Your Car Dashboard Step 3.jpg|center]]
#*You could use a sprayed surface but beware that this could cause the cookies to spread.
#Prepare the cookie dough if needed. Do either of the following:[[Image:Bake Cookies on Your Car Dashboard Step 4.jpg|center]]
#*Cut a log of pre-made cookie dough into even rounds. Place the rounds onto the cookie sheet, leaving about 1½" (4cm) of space around each cookie.

#*If you haven't purchased pre-made cookie dough, make the dough from [[Make Egg Free Refrigerator Cookies|this recipe]] (as was done for this article) or use your own cookie recipe (preferably egg-free, to avoid any potential for problems of not baking the egg sufficiently). Arrange each cookie on the baking sheet, adding blobs about tablespoon wide and leaving some space around the cookies to allow for spread.
#Place the pieces of unbaked cookie dough on the cookie sheet about 1 1/2 inches / 38mm apart.[[Image:Bake Cookies on Your Car Dashboard Step 5.jpg|center]]
#*Use a spatula or a fork to flatten the cookies, if needed. They may be fine without this.
#*Cover the cookies with plastic-wrap if not baking immediately and keep in the refrigerator until needed. Don't make the dough too far ahead of use though, use within a few hours.
=== Baking the cookies on the dashboard ===
#Place the cookies on the baking sheet into the car. Gently push into place on the dashboard.[[Image:Bake Cookies on Your Car Dashboard Step 6.jpg|center]]

#*Place a thermometer next to the cookie sheet on the dashboard. You want to make sure that your car temperature reaches at least {{convert|165|F|C|-1}} to kill any germs that were present in any raw ingredients.<ref>http://www.foodsafety.gov/keep/charts/mintemp.html</ref>

#Shut the doors and let the sun begin the baking. You can expect the cookies to begin baking immediately but unlike baking in oven, it's advised to hang around and keep an eye on things as this is far more experimental than standard baking.<ref> https://www.autoblog.com/2018/08/07/car-hack-bake-cookies-dashboard-heat/</ref>[[Image:Bake Cookies on Your Car Dashboard Step 7.jpg|center]]

#Keep an eye on the baking process by looking through the windshield regularly. The cooking time will vary depending on the temperature inside your car. Your cookies will set, but they won't brown much because the car isn't hot enough to caramelize the sugars in the cookies.[[Image:Bake Cookies on Your Car Dashboard Step 8.jpg|center]]

#Check now and then. Open the car door to check your cookies when they begin to look set. Touch the edges and the centers. The edges should be firm, and the centers should be set but not gooey.[[Image:Bake Cookies on Your Car Dashboard Step 9.jpg|center]]
#*Try to slide a cookie from the parchment paper. If the cookie is done, it will come off of the paper easily. If the cookie is not done, it will stick to the paper.
#*Close the car door if not done yet. Continue to check on the cookies every 15 to 30 minutes until they are done.

#Remove the cookie sheet from your car. Remove the cookies from the sheet with a spatula and place them on a wire rack to cool completely, although they won't be as hot as when they're removed from the oven.[[Image:Bake Cookies on Your Car Dashboard Step 10.jpg|center]]
#Finished.[[Image:Bake Cookies on Your Car Dashboard Final.jpg|center]]
== Video ==
{{Video:Bake Cookies on Your Car Dashboard|}}
== Tips ==
*Bring cookie dough in a portable refrigerator or cooler on a camping trip. You can easily bake chocolate chip cookies on your car dashboard while you swim or do other activities.
== Warnings ==
*Do not sit in the car with the cookies as they bake. Temperatures rise over 200ºF in a car on a hot day.
== Things You'll Need ==
*Cookie sheet
*Parchment paper
*Knife to slice cookies
*A car or other enclosed vehicle
*Kitchen towel
*Thermometer
*Spatula
*Wire cooling rack

added: You may be craving chocolate chip cookies on a hot day, but the last thing you want to do is fire up your oven. Take advantage of the heat and bake cookies on your car dashboard. This article provides step-by-step instructions.
#Remove any items that you may need from your car. You will have to keep your car doors and windows closed throughout the baking process.
#Line a cookie sheet with parchment paper. Avoid placing your cookie dough on a surface sprayed with nonstick spray because it may cause the cookies to spread.

#Cut a log of pre-made cookie dough into even rounds. Place the rounds onto the cookie sheet, leaving about 1-1/2" (38mm) of space around each cookie.

[[Image:A_Cookiedashboard1.jpg|center|550px]]

# Spread a kitchen towel on your dashboard and place the cookie sheet on top of the towel. Place a thermometer next to it. You want to make sure that your car temperature reaches at least 160 F (71 C) to kill any germs that were present in your raw ingredients.

[[Image:A_Cookiesdashboard2a.jpg|550px|center]]

#Keep an eye on the baking process by looking through the windshield. The cooking time will vary depending on the temperature inside your car. Your cookies will set, but they won't brown much because the car isn't hot enough to caramelize the sugars in the cookies.

[[Image:A_Cookiedashboard3.jpg|550px|thumb]]
#Open the car door to check your cookies when they begin to look set.
#*Touch the edges and the centers. The edges should be firm, and the centers should be set but not gooey.

#*Try to slide a cookie from the parchment paper. If the cookie is done, it will come off of the paper easily. If the cookie is not done, it will stick to the paper.

[[Image:A_Cookiedashboard6.jpg|550px|center]]
#Close the car door and continue to check on the cookies every 15 to 30 minutes until they are done.
#Remove the cookie sheet from your car. Remove the cookies from the sheet with a spatula and place them on a wire rack to cool completely.
#Serve your cookies with a glass of cold milk.
*Make sure the outdoor temperature is at least 95 F (35 C) before you try this project. For best results, park your car in a sunny spot.
*Bring cookie dough in a portable refrigerator or cooler on a camping trip. You can easily bake chocolate chip cookies on your car dashboard while you swim or do other activities.

== Ingredients ==
*  Pre-made cookie dough
[[Category:Baking]]
[[Category:Cookies and Biscuits]]
== Steps ==
#  Spray a cookie sheet with a can of cooking spray. (Shake before spraying!)
#  Most likely, you will be using pre-made cookie dough for baking in your car, so cut the dough into even lengths.
#  Place the pieces of un-baked cookies on your cookie sheet about 1 1/2 inches apart.
#  Use your spatula to flatten the cookies, or if you have gloves, use your fingers to.
#  Next, cover the cookies with your plastic-wrap, and keep in the refrigerator for about 30 minutes.
#  Place the cookie sheet inside of your car, on the dashboard, and put your handy thermometer next to it, so you know how hot it gets as your cookies bake!

#  It will usually take your cookies around two hours to finish baking, so look through your windshield, when this amount of time passes. When your cookies look a bit bronzed, or baked, it's time for eating!
== Tips ==
*Park your vehicle in a VERY sunny spot, so the cookies can actually bake!
*Make sure it is at least 95 degrees Fahrenheit outside.
== Warnings ==
*Do NOT stay in your vehicle while your cookies are baking. Temperatures rise over 200 degrees in a car on a hot day!
*Eating raw cookie dough can you put you at a risk of salmonella infection, from raw eggs. Try making your own cookie dough, with an egg-less recipe to avoid this high risk.
== Things You'll Need ==
*Cookie sheet
*Non-stick cooking spray
*Plastic wrap
*Spatula
*A car or other enclosed vehicle
*Thermometer
*Potholder
